title: Production of Recombinant EnvA Rabies Virus

steps_raw.instruction: Production of Recombinant EnvA Rabies Virus
Scope and Applicability: The protocol is for the large-scale production of EnvA-pseudotyped recombinant rabies virus.
HEK293T cells: (ATCC CRL-11268).

B7GG cells: B7GG cells are derived from BHK-21 cells, and stably express T7 RNA polymerase, rabies virus G and histone-tagged GFP. This cell line was described in Osakada et al. listed in section 6.0.

BHK-EnvA cells: BHK-EnvA cells are derived from BHK-21 cells, and stably express a chimeric envelope protein consisting of the extracellular and transmembrane domains of EnvA fused to the cytoplasmic domain of rabies virus G. These cells are used for pseudotyping G deleted rabies viruses with EnvA. This cell line was described in Osakada et al. in section 6.0.
HEK293-TVA cells as described in Osakada et al. in section 6.0.

Prepare DMEM with 10% FBS and 1% Antibiotic-Antimycotic by adding 50 ml of FBS and 5 ml of Antibiotic-Antimycotic to 500 ml of DMEM, and store at 4ºC
LB medium for bacteria culture should be added with antibiotics right before use.
Methodology/Procedures:
Design of recombinant rabies viruses
Clone of the transgene of interest into the G locus of Rabies CVS-N2c(ΔG)-EGFP DNA genomic plasmid.

The CVS-N2c(ΔG)-EGFP plasmid carries a deletion of the G gene and the insertion of eGFP between 5’ XmaI and 3’ NheI-KasI sites in the G gene. Other rabies CVS-N2c(ΔG) constructs are generated by replacing the eGFP gene with the transgene of interest. The Kozak sequence and the coding sequence of the transgene therefore should be flanked with restriction sites compatible with XmaI, KasI or NheI. The PCR products of the Kozak sequence and the transgene are digested with the restriction enzymes and ligated to the CVS-N2c(ΔG)-EGFP genomic plasmid digested with compatible restriction enzymes.
PCR amplify transgenes of interest using a high-fidelity polymerase and conduct PCR purification
Digest the PCR amplification products and the CVS N2c (ΔG)-EGFP plasmid with appropriate restriction enzymes
Perform electrophoresis of the digested PCR products and plasmids in 1% agarose gel/SYBR in 1X TAE buffer.
Extract the bands of interests in gel under illumination of blue light, followed by gel purification and elution into water.

Ligate the digested PCR products to the rabies viral backbone using rapid ligation kit and transform chemically competent Stb3 cells with the ligation reaction mix, followed by plating on agarose plates containing Carbenicillin.

Check colony formation on the plate after overnight incubation at 37ºC incubators. Due to the large size of rabies genomic plasmids, colonies may appear to be small after overnight incubation, and may require up to 24hr of incubation.
Pick up at least 4 colonies per plasmid to screen for the correct plasmid DNA. Start mini cultures in 2 ml of LB media containing Carbenicillin (100 μg/ml).

Plasmid DNA can be extracted from the mini cultures using a Plasmid Mini Prep Kit after overnight incubation. Restriction digest the minipreps to confirm the correct plasmids. Since the inserts are produced by PCR, 2 correct plasmids are sent for sequencing to confirm the inserts.

Maxi culture of the expected clone can be started first in 100 ml of LB media containing Carbenicillin in the morning, and then added with fresh LB media containing Carbenicillin (100 μg/ml) in the evening to make a 500 ml culture.
Maxiprep can be conducted after overnight incubation.
Recovery of CVS N2c (ΔG) virus from cDNA in B7GG cells
Cells are maintained in DMEM with 10% FBS and 1% antibiotic Antimycotic, and are kept at 37°C, and 5% CO2. Once infected by rabies virus, cells are kept at 35°C, and 3% CO2.
B7GG cells are split into 15-cm tissue culture plates one day before transfection. On the day of transfection, B7GG cells are about 60-80% confluence.

Rescue is conducted by co-transfection of 6 constructs into B7GG cells using Lipofectamine. The type and dose of the constructs for cells in 1 15-cm-plate are: 30 µg of CVS-N2c (ΔG) genomic plasmid; 15 µg of pTIT-N; 7.5 µg of pTIT-P; 7.5 µg of pTIT-L; 5 µg of pCAGGS-N2c(G); and 9 µg of T7 polymerase.
At 24 hr after transfection, cells are fed with fresh medium, and placed in an incubator at 35°C, and 3% CO2.

Cells are fed with fresh medium every 2 days, and are usually split 1:2 every 4 days. It can take up to 7 days to observe the first appearance of rescued viruses, that is, the expression of fluorescence markers encoded by the virus.
Supernatants from rescue cultures are collected upon the first appearance of cells expressing the fluorescent marker, and supernatant collection is ended 10 days after cells reach maximal infection.
Supernatant is filtered at 0.45 µm, dated, and can be stored at 4°C for weeks and at −80°C for long-term storage.

Supernatants from the recovery step are concentrated by ultracentrifugation (2 hour, 700000 rcf, SW 32 Ti, ultracentrifugation tube 326823, Beckman coulter). Each ultracentrifugation tube is loaded with 38 ml of supernatant using serological pipettes, and sealed with parafilm membrane. The viral pellet in each centrifugation tube is resuspended in 30 µl of HBSS.
Amplification of CVS N2c (ΔG) virus from cDNA in B7GG cells

B7GG cells are split into 15-cm tissue culture plates one day before amplification. On the day of experiments, B7GG cells are about 60-80% confluence. Each plate is replaced with 20 ml of fresh medium on the day of viral infection.
B7GG cells are added with viral resuspension concentrated from supernatant produced from the virus recovery step (8.2.7.). Viral suspension from 220 ml of supernatant can be added to 1 plate.
At 24 hr after transfection, cells are fed with fresh medium, and placed in an incubator at 35°C, and 3% CO2.

Cells are fed with fresh medium every 2 days, and are usually split 1:2 every 4 days. Supernatants from rescue cultures are collected upon the first appearance of cells expressing the fluorescent marker to up to 10 days after cells reach maximal infection. Supernatant is filtered at 0.45 µm, dated, and can be stored at 4°C for weeks and at −80°C for long-term storage.

The virus yield in supernatants collected on different days is tested while waiting for cells to reach maximal infection. Thirty-eight microliters of supernatants are taken from batches collected on different days, and concentrated as described in 8.2.8. The viral pellets are resuspended in 30 µl of HBSS. 293 cells are seeded into 24-well-plates the day before, and 5 µl of viral resuspension is added to each well of 293 cells. Fluorescence from rabies viruses can be observed 24-36 hr later.
Pseudotyping of CVS-N2c (ΔG) virus in BHK-EnvA cells
Cells are maintained in DMEM with 10% FBS and 1% Antibiotic-Antimycotic, and are kept at 37°C, and 5% CO2. Once infected by rabies virus, cells are kept at 35°C, and 3% CO2.

For pseudotyping, the highest possible multiplicity-of-infection (MOI) should be achieved. Ten plates of 15 cm dishes of BHK-EnvA cells are sufficient to prepare high titer viruses. Cells are split one day before, and reach 60% confluency the next day.

All 10 plates of cells are replaced with fresh medium and added with unpseudotyped G-deleted rabies virus. For unpseudotyped G-deleted rabies from B7GG cells, each plate can be added with virus from the equivalent of 50 ml of filtered supernatant.

Maintain the dishes in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2 at 37°C for overnight. The medium containing unpseudotyped viruses are then removed from infected BHK-EnvA cell dishes, the cells are rinsed 3 times with PBS and then digested with TrypLE to remove unpseudotyped viruses. Cells are split into 20 new plates, and placed in 3% CO2 at 35°C overnight.
The media are removed again on the next day, and replaced with 20 ml of fresh medium.
The culture supernatant is then collected every 2 days and cells are split when reaching 90% confluency. Three batches of supernatants are collected from BHK-EnvA cells infected with rabies viruses.
Each batch of supernatant is filtered through a 0.45 μm filter, and kept at 4C. The supernatant batches are then concentrated as concentrated as described in 8.2.8.

Concentrated viruses from step 8.4.7 can be further concentrated by undergone another step of ultracentrifugation. Virus from step 8.4.7 is loaded into ultracentrifugation tubes 344624, the tubes are sealed with parafilm membrane, and undergone 2 hr of centrifugation at 70,000 g using the SW 60 Ti rotor. The pellets are re-dissolved in 100-500 µl of HBSS.
Measuring the titer of EnvA CVS-N2c (ΔG) virus in HEK293-TVA cells

To titer pseudotyped viruses from step 8.4.8, a full plate of HEK293-TVA cells in a 15-cm plate is digested using TrypLE and resuspended in 10 ml of fresh medium. Two milliliter of the cell suspension is then diluted using 10 ml of fresh medium and each well of a 24-well plate is seeded with 500 μl of the cell suspension.
On the next day, make a tenfold serial dilution of the viral preparation (from a dilution of 10−3 to a dilution of 10−8) of the viral preparation. The following dilutions can be tested:

Add 250 μl of each viral dilution (A–F) to the cells gently (final medium volume: 750 µl). Triplicate wells are prepared for each dilution. The cells are then returned to an incubator with 3% CO2 at 35°C. The rabies-encoded fluorescence should become visible 24–36 h after infection.
Three days after the initial infection, determine the number of infected cells and calculate the biological titer (infectious units/ml).
Clean the hood with 70% Ethanol after use.
The biohazard waste generated during the process is disposed according to the biohazard waste procedure guidelines.
Technical Information:
Tubes for ultracentrifugation need to be weighted before loading to the ultracentrifuge. The difference in weight between tubes is controlled to be less than 0.05 g.
